title: AI Unlocked: Entrepreneurship
blurb: Start or boost a business with AI: the entrepreneurial mindset, Business Model Canvas, SOSTAC strategy, platform-smart digital marketing, the RSCF prompt formula, and a 30-day launch plan with ROI tracking. Taught from the Team21 playbook used across two continents.

modules.d: Your WHY, problem-first thinking, and smart startup finance.
modules.body:
Every business begins in the mind

Before tools, platforms, or strategies: why do you want to build a business, and how do you think about problems, money, and growth?

Start with your WHY — the Golden Circle

  • WHY — your purpose, cause, or belief. Why does your business exist beyond money?
  • HOW — your unique approach, process, or values.
  • WHAT — the products or services you actually sell.

Most entrepreneurs start with WHAT and forget WHY. Start with WHY — a business built on authentic purpose attracts loyal customers, dedicated teammates, and long-term sustainability.

Reflection questions

  • What problem in your community genuinely bothers you?
  • If money were not an issue, what business would you still run?
  • What value do you want to be known for in 5 years?

Problems are your business

What frustrates people daily? What takes too long or costs too much? What do people wish existed? What local gaps do you notice? A specific painful problem beats a clever product every time.

Finance basics — from zero to above

  • Rule 1: start with your own money, even if small — skin in the game sharpens thinking.
  • Rule 2: only invest what you're willing to lose in your first 90 days.
  • Rule 3: get a coach or mentor who has already made the mistakes for you — pay them if necessary.
ROI = (Revenue − Investment) ÷ Investment × 100. Target a minimum of 10%; well-targeted digital businesses routinely do far better in month one. Track it from day one.
Kai-Fu Lee (AI Superpowers) calls this the age of implementation: the advantage has shifted from those who invent AI to those who apply it fastest to real problems. That is precisely an entrepreneur’s game — and this playbook is your implementation manual.

quiz.q: In the Golden Circle, most entrepreneurs mistakenly start with…

modules.d: All 9 blocks, explained with worked examples.
modules.body:
Your business on one page

The BMC (Alexander Osterwalder) answers three questions across nine blocks: Who do we serve? What value do we deliver? How do we capture money doing it?

  • 1. Customer Segments — WHO are you serving? Be painfully specific: "busy parents aged 25–40 in my metro area who need event flyers this week" beats "everyone."
  • 2. Value Proposition — WHY do they choose you? Combine speed, quality, and price to dominate a niche: "professional flyers designed in 30 minutes for $15."
  • 3. Channels — HOW do they find you? Business messaging catalog, community groups, Instagram reels at peak hours, physical flyers with QR codes.
  • 4. Customer Relationships — HOW do you build trust? Follow-up after purchase, loyalty rewards, broadcast/SMS lists, referral bonuses, community groups.
  • 5. Revenue Streams: per-item fees, bundles, monthly subscriptions, affiliate commissions, training fees.
  • 6. Key Resources: smartphone, Canva, an AI assistant, design templates, a payments account, a testimonials portfolio.
  • 7. Key Activities: design, client communication, content posting, order processing, quality control, performance tracking.
  • 8. Key Partnerships: print shops, photographers, payment agents, other freelancers, community leaders.
  • 9. Cost Structure: fixed (subscriptions, data) vs variable (payment fees ~2–3%, printing per order).

Complete worked example — "QuickDesign"

Segments: event organizers, churches, families, small businesses. Value: professional flyers in 30 minutes, bilingual EN/FR. Channels: messaging catalog + community groups + reels. Relationships: follow-ups, loyalty discounts, referrals. Revenue: per-flyer, bundles, a 10-flyer monthly subscription. Resources: Canva, AI, smartphone, templates, testimonials. Activities: design, comms, content, tracking. Partnerships: print shops, photographers. Costs: subscriptions + per-transaction fees.

AI prompt: "Act as a business strategy expert. Help me create a complete Business Model Canvas for my [type of business]. Ask me clarifying questions about my customers, value proposition, revenue model, resources, and partnerships. Present the completed BMC in a clear 9-block format."
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as a business coach for my market. Ask me 5 deep questions, one at a time, to uncover my entrepreneurial WHY from my skills, passions, and the problems around me. Then summarize my WHY in one powerful sentence and propose the single niche where it meets paying demand.

quiz.q: Which BMC block answers "WHY do customers choose YOU"?

modules.d: Situation → Objectives → Strategy → Tactics → Action → Control.
modules.body:
SOSTAC at a glance

Developed by PR Smith; one of the world's most used planning frameworks. Six steps from analysis to measurement:

  • S — Situation: where are we NOW? Run a SWOT: strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats. Ask AI to analyze your market: "Identify 5 market opportunities, 3 key competitors, major customer pain points, relevant digital trends, and economic factors — as a structured SWOT."
  • O — Objectives: SMART goals. Examples: "$1,500 in sales by Day 30" · "30 new paying customers in Month 1" · "grow my broadcast list to 200 contacts in 4 weeks" · "post 3× weekly for 4 weeks."
  • S — Strategy: the big picture — your OFFER (niche beats general), your PLATFORM (where your audience actually is), your PEOPLE (exactly who your ideal customer is and what they need most).
  • T — Tactics: the specific actions — teasers, status posts, bilingual visual content, countdowns, platform-native formats.
  • A — Action: who does what by when. Day 1: business profile + catalog live. Day 2: launch flyer with Canva + AI. Day 3: post in 10+ community groups. Day 5: DM 20 prospects, convert 3. Day 7: educational content. Day 10: first 3 testimonials. Day 14: referral promo. Day 21: review data and adjust. Day 30: revenue vs SMART targets.
  • C — Control: a simple tracking table — Date · Platform · Content posted · Responses · Revenue · Lesson learned. What gets measured gets improved.
Mega prompt: "Build a complete SOSTAC plan for my [type of business]. S — 3 key situation insights; O — 3 SMART objectives; S — my positioning strategy; T — a 2-week tactics calendar; A — a 10-item action checklist; C — 5 KPIs to track weekly."

quiz.q: A goal that is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound is called…

modules.d: Meet your market where it lives — with real platform data and tactics.
modules.body:
Principle: local beats copied

Digital marketing is not about copying what works somewhere else — it's about understanding YOUR audience's daily platform habits. We teach with real market data; here is the playbook and how to localize it.

The platform selection questions

  • Where does my exact segment spend daily time?
  • What content format converts there (groups? reels? DMs? articles)?
  • What is the realistic ROI pattern, and when is peak engagement?

Field data from our home market (keep for global clients)

  • Messaging-first commerce (WhatsApp): ~95% of smartphone users; 3× conversion vs email; catalogs, broadcast lists, voice notes, QR codes on everything. The playbook: complete business profile → product catalog → auto-replies → segmented broadcast lists → daily status promos.
  • Facebook: dominant across ages; community groups + click-to-chat ads; ~300% ROI when geo-targeted.
  • TikTok: explosive youth reach; challenges + shop; small campaigns have returned ~670% ROI.
  • Instagram: style-conscious 18–35; reels at ~7 PM peak.
  • LinkedIn: B2B services, training, consulting — thought leadership converts professionals.

US market localization

  • Messaging-first behavior lives in SMS/iMessage and email lists — build an email list from day one (it's the WhatsApp of the US market: owned, direct, high-conversion).
  • LinkedIn is the primary B2B engine; Instagram/TikTok for consumer reach; Google Business Profile + reviews replace market-stall visibility; Facebook groups still convert for local services.
  • Keep the same discipline: pick 2 platforms, post consistently, drive everything to a channel you own.
AI prompt: "Write 5 auto-reply templates for my [type of business]: welcome, pricing FAQ, order confirmation, out-of-hours, and a warm follow-up for cold leads. Professional, warm, bilingual EN/FR."

quiz.q: The single most important marketing asset to build from day one in any market is…

modules.t: AI Tools & Content Creation: The RSCF Formula
modules.d: Your AI toolkit and the Team21 prompt structure for great results.
modules.body:
The great equalizer

AI tools let a single entrepreneur with a smartphone produce marketing content, professional copy, designs, and analysis at zero or minimal cost.

Your AI toolkit

  • ChatGPT — writing, business plans, BMC, SOSTAC, social content
  • Claude — long-form analysis, reports, strategy documents
  • Canva — flyers, carousels, logos, social graphics
  • CapCut — video editing, reels, subtitles
  • Copilot — Office integration, Excel analysis
  • Gemini / AI Studio — research, Google Workspace integration, power features
  • Remove.bg — clean product photos in seconds

The RSCF prompt formula

  • R — ROLE: tell AI who to be. "Act as a marketing expert for small businesses…"
  • S — SITUATION: give context. "…I am launching a flyer design service with a $500 budget…"
  • C — COMMAND: a clear task. "…Write a 7-day content calendar…"
  • F — FORMAT: specify the output. "…as a table with Day, Caption, Platform, and Goal."

Content templates that convert

  • Flyer caption: benefit + urgency + price. "Want your next event poster to stand out? Designed in 30 minutes for $15. DM now — limited weekend slots!"
  • 3-slide carousel: (1) "Why your event flyer isn't getting attention" (2) "3 design mistakes to avoid" (3) "Let me fix it — DM to book yours."
  • Status/story posts: rotate curiosity, social proof, urgency, education, storytelling — under 60 words.
  • Teasers: "New design style dropping soon… 2 days to go."
  • CTAs that close: "Send the name + event details and I'll start now." · "Want it ready in 30 minutes? Lock in your slot." · "Payment link ready — shall I send?"

quiz.q: In RSCF, the "F" tells the AI…

modules.d: Knowledge without action is entertainment — launch in 30 days.
modules.body:
The launch checklist — Week 0 (before you launch)

  • Complete your BMC (all 9 blocks) and define 3 SMART objectives for Month 1.
  • Set up your business profiles: messaging/business account with catalog and auto-replies, plus your chosen social page.
  • Design your launch flyer with Canva + AI copy; prepare your first 7 days of content.
  • Set up your ROI tracking sheet; identify 3 network contacts who will support your launch.

Week 1 — LAUNCH (Days 1–7)

  • Day 1: launch announcement on all platforms.
  • Day 2: post in 10+ community groups.
  • Day 3: DM 30 warm contacts.
  • Day 5: follow up with non-responders.
  • Day 7: post your first customer testimonial; review Days 1–7 performance.

Weeks 2–4 — OPTIMIZE & SCALE

  • Launch a "refer a friend" incentive; double down on the content type generating the most revenue.
  • Introduce a second service tier or upsell.
  • Calculate final Month-1 ROI vs your SMART objectives; plan Month 2 from real data.

The ROI tracker

Weekly rows: Revenue · Costs · Net Profit · ROI% · Top action. Total it at month end. This one table is the difference between a business and a hobby.

Capstone: submit your completed BMC, SOSTAC plan, launch flyer, first content week, and Week-1 tracker to your mentor. Then — launch. Done beats perfect.
